clue.text: Find business returning in the eleventh hour

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the word is read right to left
one piece placed in another sits inside it, wrapped by the outer letters

blocks.note: at the eleventh hour means late, at the last moment
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: Someone tracking down a firm that is coming back to them at the very last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed business abbreviation goes inside LATE: L-OC-ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to discover where it is, a straightforward synonym of find.

clue.text: Dial up support? That's cool!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the word read backwards
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Phone for help? A relaxed response.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid-back describes someone relaxed and unflustered, which is the slang sense of cool.

clue.text: Prisoner discovered in defeat

blocks.note: con is short for convict
found means discovered

explanation.surface: A convict is caught after losing out.
explanation.definitionFit: To confound an enemy or plan is to frustrate or overthrow it, an older sense of defeat.

clue.text: Weary of being fully dressed, but not at first

indicators.note: but not says a piece is to be left out
first says where the excluded part sits, at the very start

blocks.note: attired means clothed
the word itself, removed from the front

explanation.surface: Someone fed up with always being in formal clothes, though not originally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is used literally: the two letters A and T come off the front of ATTIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired and weary are both adjectives for someone exhausted or lacking energy.

clue.text: Doctored cocain's gained nothing in the event

indicators.note: a doctored substance has been tampered with, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the letters of the word as printed, apostrophe dropped
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Cut drugs turn out to be worthless at the party.
explanation.walkthrough: The cocaine is deliberately misspelt as cocain's so its letters, plus O, rearrange exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion is a particular happening or function, so it is a synonym of event.

clue.text: London landlord's initial

blocks.note: London is the capital city of England
a landlord is one who lets property

explanation.surface: The first name of a London pub owner.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the landlord is also the keeper of a pub, so 'initial' suggests his first letter of name.
explanation.definitionFit: An initial is the large first letter of a name or paragraph, written as an upper-case letter.

clue.text: Difficult period in which to adapt to Bach medley

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture of tunes, so these letters are jumbled together

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An arranger struggles to rework a selection of Bach pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Going through a bad patch is an idiom for a spell of trouble or poor form.

clue.text: Surrounding pupils with flowers

blocks.note: first meaning: the coloured rings around the pupils of the eyes
second meaning: plants with sword-shaped leaves and showy blooms

explanation.surface: A classroom decorated all round with blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupils' suggests schoolchildren, but these are the dark centres of the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the coloured parts of the eye ringing each pupil and a family of garden flowers.

clue.text: Dan got up to eat scrambled egg, but was scolded

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the name is read from the bottom upwards
scrambling mixes things up, so these letters are rearranged
what eats something takes it inside

blocks.note: the name read backwards
the letters of egg rearranged

explanation.surface: Dan rose late for scrambled eggs at breakfast and got told off.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag is to criticise or complain at someone persistently, so nagged is a synonym of scolded.

clue.text: Core section of problems certain nervous patients exhibit

indicators.note: a section is a slice taken out of a longer run of text
the words exhibit, or show, what lies within them

blocks.note: found across the end of certain and the start of nervous

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist describing the central difficulty that anxious patients display.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across certaIN NERvous.
explanation.definitionFit: Core and inner both describe the central, innermost part of something, so they are adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Fetching from a very quiet London borough

blocks.note: taken as written
pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet
Ealing is a borough in west London

explanation.surface: Something attractive comes from a peaceful corner of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' looks like a verb (collecting from somewhere) but is the adjective meaning attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching and appealing are both adjectives meaning attractive or charming.

clue.text: You should not have to wait too long for only this

definitions.text: You should not have to wait too long for only this

blocks.clueFragment: You should not have to wait too long for only this
blocks.note: surface reading: a vague complaint about how long something takes

blocks.clueFragment: You should not have to wait too long for only this
blocks.note: setter's reading: the phrase that, preceded by 'only', means something is bound to happen soon

explanation.walkthrough: The word 'only' is the key: the answer completes the stock phrase meaning something inevitable will come before long.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is only this means it is certain to happen eventually, so the wait will not be long.

clue.text: American woman obtains actors for programme

blocks.note: broad is American slang for a woman
the cast is the actors in a production

explanation.surface: An American actress hires a company of performers for her show.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast is a radio or television programme, so the noun is a synonym.

clue.text: Part of cooked recipe not right

indicators.note: not marks something that must be left out of the word
cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right, removed

explanation.surface: A cook admits a section of the dish went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R out of RECIPE and rearrange the remaining five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion or bit of something, a direct synonym of part.

clue.text: Go with a reluctant sort to offer good wishes

indicators.note: to sort things is to arrange them in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Accompanying an unwilling person so as to pass on best wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' reads as a noun (a reluctant sort of person) but is the verb signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To congratulate someone is to express pleasure at their success, a way of offering good wishes.

clue.text: Note: cover required for moving to a new home

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a housing is a protective casing or cover

explanation.surface: A memo saying insurance is needed for a house move.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes 'Note' look like a heading; it is the musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehousing is providing people with new accommodation, i.e. moving them somewhere new to live.

clue.text: Greed shown by Roman love god with sex appeal! Why?

indicators.note: the question word, spoken, matches the name of a single letter

blocks.note: Cupid is the Roman god of love
it is old slang for sex appeal
the letter name is said the same as this question word

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about why the god of love is so alluring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' for sex appeal comes from the 1927 film 'It' starring Clara Bow, the 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupidity is a formal word for avarice, an excessive desire for wealth or possessions.

clue.text: Fish dish, a combination of French and Greek cooking for Edward

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: apparently read as a one-letter 'and', though French uses et
taken as written
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A rice dish blending French and Greek cuisine made for a man called Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: GREEK and ED supply only seven of the eight letters, one E short; the extra E seems meant to come from 'French and', which is loose since French 'and' is et.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is an Anglo-Indian dish of flaked smoked fish, rice and eggs, often eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Rent building for a monastery

blocks.note: to charter is to hire or rent a vessel or vehicle
a house is a building

explanation.surface: Leasing premises to be used by monks.
explanation.walkthrough: A Charterhouse is a Carthusian monastery; the London one later gave its name to a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Charterhouse is the English name for a monastery of the Carthusian order.

clue.text: Mother over time gets hurt

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece on top of, so before, the second

blocks.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Over the years a mother ends up injured.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage and hurt are both nouns for harm done to someone or something.

clue.text: Somehow slipped quietly off to drive away

indicators.note: taking something off removes it from the word
somehow says the letters end up arranged in some other way

blocks.note: taken as written
p, piano, is the musical marking for quietly; one is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone sneaked away in silence in order to drive off.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one P from SLIPPED and rearrange the six letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel doubts or a crowd is to scatter them or make them go away.

clue.text: A last word for the French

definitions.text: A last word for the French

blocks.clueFragment: A last word for the French
blocks.note: surface reading: the French people get the final say in something

blocks.clueFragment: A last word for the French
blocks.note: setter's reading: what French speakers say on parting for good, their farewell

explanation.walkthrough: 'Last word' suggests having the final say; here it is literally the final word said on leaving, in French.
explanation.definitionFit: This French farewell, used when one does not expect to meet again, is literally a last word of goodbye.

clue.text: On the increase if tangent deflected

indicators.note: something deflected is knocked off course, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A geometry line that grows when knocked aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fattening means growing larger or plumper, so it describes something on the increase.

clue.text: Fairy-like or fish-like appendage the Spanish found first

indicators.note: being found first means coming at the front of the answer

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
a fin is a limb-like part on a fish

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether a creature's limb resembles a fairy's or a fish's, first spotted in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means like an elf, small and delicate, and elves are fairy folk.

clue.text: I impel RAF to produce an electronic device

indicators.note: the letters are made to produce something new by being rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Royal Air Force abbreviation, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone pushes the air force into inventing a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: An amplifier is an electronic unit that boosts the strength of a signal.

clue.text: Monarch follows fair foreign monk

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so the letters take an altered form
one piece follows, so it comes after the other in the answer

blocks.note: the letters of fair rearranged
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A king trails behind a light-skinned holy man from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a member of a mendicant religious order, close enough to a monk for a crossword.

clue.text: People are usually too late to hear these words of praise about them

definitions.text: People are usually too late to hear these words of praise about them

blocks.clueFragment: People are usually too late to hear these words of praise about them
blocks.note: surface reading: compliments that arrive after people have stopped listening

blocks.clueFragment: People are usually too late to hear these words of praise about them
blocks.note: setter's reading: tributes spoken at funerals, when the subject is dead, the late

explanation.walkthrough: 'Too late' puns on 'the late', meaning deceased: such tributes are given at a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: These are speeches or writings praising someone, typically someone who has just died.

clue.text: Enemy organisation captures unknown catalyst

indicators.note: organising something puts it into a new arrangement
what captures something holds it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
x, y and z are the unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: A hostile group takes a mysterious figure prisoner, triggering events.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange ENEMY with Z inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An enzyme is a protein that speeds up a chemical reaction in the body, a biological catalyst.
